children: Foreign portfolio investors (FPIs), who turned net buyers of Indian equities in August for the second consecutive month after seven months of sustained selling, stepped up buying in Financial Services and Consumer Services, betting on segments where valuations have moderated following the recent market selloff.

The two sectors together attracted close to $2 billion in FPI inflows in August, accounting for nearly 64% of the total $3.1 billion that overseas investors pumped into Indian equities during the month, data compiled by the National Securities Depository Ltd. (NSDL) showed.

The buying was led by Financial Services, with overseas investors also raising their exposure to Consumer Services, which includes consumer-facing segments such as hotels and other discretionary businesses. Market participants said the recent correction has made valuations in these areas more attractive, prompting FPIs to return to segments that had seen significant selling pressure earlier.

Healthcare was the third-largest beneficiary of FPI flows, attracting about $622 million during the month, according to NSDL data. Information Technology followed with inflows of around $430 million, while Consumer Durables saw overseas investors purchase stocks worth approximately $410 million.

The buying comes against the backdrop of a broader recovery in risk appetite following the prolonged selloff in Indian equities. The benchmark Nifty50 is currently trading at less than 18 times 12-month forward earnings, below its five-year average of around 20 times, according to Bloomberg data.

Mid- and small-cap stocks, however, outperformed large caps in August. The Nifty Midcap index gained more than 2%, while the Nifty Smallcap index rose over 3% during the month, compared with a 1.2% decline in the Nifty50.

“FPI selling has been a key reason behind the underperformance of large caps, and some of these FPI flows could return to large caps,” said George Joseph, CIO & CEO (Equity) at ASK Investment Managers.

Financial Services continues to remain the largest sector in the FPI portfolio. The sector accounted for 30.1% of total FPI equity holdings of $737 billion at the end of August, equivalent to about 14.3% of India's $5.2 trillion equity market capitalisation.

On the other hand, Telecommunication witnessed the highest FPI selling in August, with overseas investors offloading stocks worth around $522 million. FMCG and Oil & Gas followed, with outflows of about $200 million each.

India also remained among the leading emerging markets attracting foreign capital during the month. Taiwan received the highest foreign inflows at $9.1 billion, followed by India at $3.1 billion, according to Bloomberg data. South Korea, which had attracted substantial foreign investment during the AI-led rally, recorded the highest outflows among emerging markets at $8.6 billion in August.

title: Where foreign investors are putting their money after the market selloff
